definitions.objective: The TEKS-based learning students will explain, analyze, evaluate, apply, justify, or revise. It is not merely the task or artifact.
definitions.demonstration_of_learning: The project, performance, submission, revision, or concise response through which the teacher observes evidence of mastery. In this project-based course, the core activity is usually the demonstration of learning.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AI Ethics Council Day 2 — Follow the Incentive
records.objective: Students will analyze how a recommendation system's incentives distribute benefits and visibility, then justify a rule change and its tradeoff.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Casebook stakeholder map, redesigned recommendation rule, and explanation of who gains, who loses, and what new problem may result.
records.evidence_basis: The student task names what a system maximizes, maps direct and indirect stakeholders, and evaluates the consequences of a changed rule.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AI Ethics Council Day 3 — Test the Consequence
records.objective: Students will analyze a data-collection scenario for consent, benefit, harm, and appeal, then propose a safeguard matched to the identified threat.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Casebook two-sided analysis that names collected data, a helpful use, a harmful use, and one targeted safeguard.
records.evidence_basis: Students analyze a real-world privacy or surveillance scenario and propose a way to prevent the named harm.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AI Ethics Council Day 4 — Leave the Page and Check
records.objective: Students will apply lateral-reading search strategies to evaluate a digital claim's source, evidence, and level of confidence.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Casebook four-move verification trail and a verified, misleading, altered/generated, or uncertain decision supported by evidence.
records.evidence_basis: Students leave the original page, investigate the publisher, trace evidence to an earlier source, and explain a confidence decision.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AI Ethics Council Day 5 — Prepare Every Seat
records.objective: Students will analyze how an AI decision affects stakeholders with different needs, evidence, power, and ability to appeal, then justify a recommendation.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Casebook six-role hearing map with each role's need, evidence, impact, power and appeal route, plus one justified use decision and tradeoff.
audit_issues: The current §126.19(c)(8)(B) claim requires publishing a formal digital communication for a global audience; the class hearing map is not published globally.
The objective describes mapping tasks more than the learning about stakeholder power and impact.
records.evidence_basis: The task uses scholarly AI-ethics terminology in a written analysis and requires a recommendation after comparing six stakeholder positions.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AI Ethics Council Day 6 — Tasks, Not Headlines
records.objective: Students will evaluate which job tasks are appropriate for humans, AI, or a combined team and justify quality checks, accountability, and worker protections.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Casebook task map for six job tasks with human/AI assignments, quality checks, accountable people, and two justified worker or user protections.
audit_issues: The current §126.19(c)(9)(D) claim is about bias in digital information sources, but this lesson evaluates job-task allocation rather than source bias.
The objective describes the task map rather than the learning about responsible automation.
records.evidence_basis: The written sample requires accurate technology terminology and an evidence-based judgment about automation, responsibility, and safeguards.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AI Ethics Council Day 7 — Build the Assigned Role’s Case
records.objective: Students will evaluate traceable evidence from an assigned stakeholder perspective and defend a claim with reasoning, a rebuttal, and a testable safeguard.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed role brief and opening statement with a claim, two traceable evidence points, reasoning, rebuttal, cross-question, and safeguard or stopping rule.
audit_issues: §126.19(c)(8)(B) requires publication to a global audience, which the classroom role brief does not provide.
The current objective is a list of argument parts rather than the learning about evaluating and defending an evidence-based position.
records.evidence_basis: The task elicits a formal written and spoken sample using technical and ethical terminology, but it does not publish to a global audience.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AI Ethics Council Day 8 — Listen for the Evidence
records.objective: Students will evaluate competing stakeholder claims, respond to evidence-based objections, and justify a personal verdict that may differ from an assigned role.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Role brief, hearing notes that capture each role's claim and evidence, one answered objection, and a personal-verdict reflection.
audit_issues: The current §126.19(c)(8)(B) and (8)(C) claims require global digital publication or collaboration; the classroom hearing does not provide that evidence.
The objective should name the deliberation learning rather than only the hearing actions.
records.evidence_basis: The classroom hearing provides scholarly dialogue and written evidence analysis, but not global digital publication.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AI Ethics Council Day 9 — Turn Values into Testable Rules
records.objective: Students will analyze the difference between vague values and enforceable policy by specifying the responsible actor, required action, evidence connection, and compliance check.
records.demonstration_of_learning: A five-principle group code in which every rule names an actor, action, evidence connection, and method for checking compliance.
audit_issues: §126.19(c)(8)(B) requires formal digital publication for a global audience, which the group policy draft does not show.
The objective focuses on producing five rules instead of understanding what makes a policy enforceable.
records.evidence_basis: The written code uses AI ethics terminology and requires students to convert concepts such as bias, privacy, transparency, and accountability into testable language.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AI Ethics Council Day 10 — Test the Code
records.objective: Students will evaluate whether an AI policy handles new cases, apply peer feedback to revise a weak rule, and justify the final verdict with evidence.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Peer-feedback record, one documented rule revision with its evidence, individual synthesis, and final group code.
audit_issues: The current §126.19(c)(8)(B) claim requires global publication, which the group code and classroom feedback do not establish.
The objective states revision actions but should foreground evaluation of a rule's effectiveness.
records.evidence_basis: Students share a text artifact, seek feedback, revise it, and explain the evidence that changed their thinking.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: RVR Day 1 — Draw, Plan, Program, Prove
records.objective: Students will compare Draw, Blocks, and Text programming modes, select a suitable mode for a drawing task, and improve a robot program from test evidence.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Program-mode explanation, completed drawing mission sheet, initial and revised run evidence, final program screenshot, and revision claim.
records.evidence_basis: The Learn page compares modes; the drawing mission requires planning, running, revising, rerunning, and explaining what improved.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: RVR Day 2 — Precision Movement Lab
records.objective: Students will analyze how heading, speed, duration, distance, wait, and continue affect RVR movement and use test data to justify a precision revision.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Seven documented movement tests, required screenshots, and one precision claim supported by measured results.
records.evidence_basis: The lab varies movement variables one at a time, compares outcomes, and requires an evidence-based precision claim.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: RVR Day 3 — Sense, Decide, Respond
records.objective: Students will explain and apply the input, decision, and output relationship to debug a color-sensor route.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Route and code evidence, expected-versus-actual test results, a revised program, and an input-decision-output explanation.
records.evidence_basis: The Learn page explicitly teaches the systems relationship; the mission requires coding, testing, recording results, and revising.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: RVR Days 4–5 — Talking Robots School-of-Fish
records.objective: Students will analyze how shared channels, message timing, and spacing control coordinated RVR behavior and revise leader/follower programs from test evidence.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Leader and follower code, coordinated-run evidence, and a revision claim explaining the timing or spacing change.
records.evidence_basis: Teams program sender and follower behaviors, test formation, revise timing or spacing, and film the improved run.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 1 Intro to micro:bit and Block Coding
records.objective: Students will explain how block instructions become a running micro:bit output and apply the correct tool-transfer workflow to run a program on the device.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed Lesson 1 worksheet, a program running on the micro:bit, and checkpoint evidence explaining the block-to-device workflow.
audit_issues: The objective describes writing and transferring the first program rather than what students learn about the programming workflow.
§126.19(c)(1)(E) requires developing, comparing, and improving algorithms; the available evidence shows a first program but not comparison and improvement.
records.evidence_basis: The Do page requires a first block program and transfer to a physical micro:bit; the worksheet and checkpoint document the learning.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 2 Inputs and Outputs
records.objective: Students will explain how an input triggers an observable output in a micro:bit system and apply that relationship in a working program.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed Lesson 2 worksheet, a working input/output program, and checkpoint response identifying the input, program response, and output.
audit_issues: The objective describes the build; it should state the input/output systems understanding.
§126.19(c)(1)(E) is not fully evidenced because the lesson does not require comparing and improving algorithms.
records.evidence_basis: The student task explicitly pairs an input with an output and requires the program to run on the physical device.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 3 Radio and If Statements
records.objective: Students will explain how a shared radio channel and conditional rule control a micro:bit's response, then apply both concepts in a two-device message system.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed Lesson 3 worksheet, working sender and receiver programs, and checkpoint evidence explaining the message condition and resulting response.
audit_issues: The objective describes programming tasks instead of the learning about communication and conditional response.
The available assignment evidence does not explicitly require modification of previously written code, so §126.19(c)(2)(C) is overclaimed.
records.evidence_basis: The assignment requires students to program a micro:bit radio message and use an if statement; the worksheet and checkpoint capture the system explanation.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 4 Coding Games on the micro:bit
records.objective: Students will apply iterative algorithm development to design, test, and improve an original micro:bit game and explain its rules.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed game worksheet, working Rock Paper Scissors program, original-game program, test or revision evidence, and checkpoint.
audit_issues: The current objective names two builds; it should state the algorithm-development and revision learning that the original game demonstrates.
records.evidence_basis: Students implement a model game, then modify and extend the learned code patterns to design and test an original game.

records.module_name: SW5 · AIR Unit 1: Leaving Land (micro:bit + MakeCode)
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Leaving Land Lesson 1 — Seasick with Empathy
records.objective: Students will analyze evidence from a user interview to define a specific need and write a problem statement that can guide a technology solution.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed empathy map and a problem statement that identifies the user, need, evidence, and design direction.
audit_issues: The objective lists interview and planning actions rather than the learning about using evidence to define a user need.
records.evidence_basis: The student task requires interviewing, mapping what the user says and experiences, and converting evidence into a problem statement.

records.module_name: SW5 · AIR Unit 1: Leaving Land (micro:bit + MakeCode)
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Leaving Land Lesson 2 — micro:bit Light Meter
records.objective: Students will analyze how light-level data changes across conditions and explain how a threshold turns a sensor reading into a programmed response.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed light-meter program and worksheet with readings from at least two conditions, a chosen threshold, and an explanation of the resulting response.
audit_issues: The objective describes programming and testing actions but does not state the sensor-data learning.
The current §126.19(c)(2)(C) claim is not supported unless students modify previously written code; that evidence is not explicit.
records.evidence_basis: The assignment requires students to compare light readings across conditions and decide how dark is dark enough for the code.

records.module_name: SW5 · AIR Unit 1: Leaving Land (micro:bit + MakeCode)
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Leaving Land Lesson 3 — Crab Cruisin'
records.objective: Students will apply an iterative design process to plan a micro:bit game, observe a new player's experience, and revise the game from usability evidence.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Playable game, completed worksheet, partner playtest notes, and one documented revision based on observed confusion.
records.evidence_basis: The task requires planning win and loss rules, building, silent partner testing, observing confusion, and revising the program.

records.module_name: SW5 · AIR Unit 1: Leaving Land (micro:bit + MakeCode)
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Leaving Land Lesson 4 — Ocean Games
records.objective: Students will apply prior MakeCode Arcade knowledge to implement playable rules, test the complete game, and improve an algorithm or rule that does not work as intended.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed ocean game and worksheet with a full playthrough plus one documented bug, rule change, or fix.
audit_issues: The objective and DOL focus on game completion; they do not identify what the finished game proves about algorithm development or debugging.
records.evidence_basis: The assignment asks students to build from an existing worksheet route, play the complete game, fix what breaks, and submit the worksheet.

records.module_name: SW5 · AIR Unit 1: Leaving Land (micro:bit + MakeCode)
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Leaving Land Lesson 5 — AI Enemies
records.objective: Students will explain how repeated decision rules create rule-based game AI and apply those rules to tune an enemy that is challenging but beatable.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Ocean game with a reactive enemy, playtest evidence showing difficulty tuning, and an explanation of the enemy's repeated rules.
records.evidence_basis: The student page distinguishes rule-based AI from learned models and requires implementation, repeated playtesting, tuning, and explanation.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Sailing Home Lesson 1 — Conflicting Viewpoints
records.objective: Students will analyze how two digital sources use evidence and omissions to support conflicting claims, then justify which conclusions the available evidence supports.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed AEIOU organizer plus a concise comparison naming each source's claim and evidence, one omission, and a justified evidence judgment.
audit_issues: The objective names use of the AEIOU organizer rather than the source-evaluation learning.
The DOL names only completion and does not require the comparative judgment needed to prove mastery.
records.evidence_basis: The assignment presents two opposing ocean-plastic articles and explicitly asks students to note what each text includes and leaves out.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Sailing Home Lesson 2 — Temperature Bot
records.topic: Sensor data, thresholds, and robot response
records.objective: Students will explain how a temperature reading becomes an input, how a coded threshold makes a decision, and how that decision controls RVR behavior.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed worksheet, functioning temperature bot, code and readings, and a short input-threshold-output explanation.
audit_issues: The objective describes mounting, coding, and testing; it should state the learning about how sensor data and threshold logic control behavior.
records.evidence_basis: The assignment explicitly teaches that the sensor reports a number and the code decides which readings trigger the robot response.

records.module_name: SW5 · Save the Day with Smart Electronics
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 1 Wiring LEDs with micro:bit Expansion Board
records.objective: Students will explain how pin assignments and timing control circuit outputs and apply troubleshooting evidence to correct a traffic-light sequence.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Traffic-light worksheet, working build, checkpoint, and one documented fault, test, or correction connecting wiring or code to the output.
audit_issues: The objective states the wiring and build rather than the learning about outputs, sequencing, and troubleshooting.
records.evidence_basis: The assignment requires three wired LED outputs, a timed sequence, live-build troubleshooting, and a checkpoint on wiring and code.

records.module_name: SW5 · Save the Day with Smart Electronics
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 2 Wiring and Programming Inputs
records.objective: Students will analyze how a physical button input and debounce logic produce one reliable state change, then apply troubleshooting to correct repeated presses.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Possession-arrow worksheet, working build, checkpoint, and evidence that one button press produces one explained state change.
audit_issues: The objective states the button and possession-arrow build rather than the learning about reliable physical input and debouncing.
records.evidence_basis: The task explicitly identifies the multiple-press fault and requires students to fix it in code by waiting for the press to end.

records.module_name: SW5 · Save the Day with Smart Electronics
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 3 Servo Motors
records.objective: Students will explain how a light-sensor threshold controls servo position and use test evidence to refine the sunshade's response.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Sunshade worksheet, working build, checkpoint, recorded light and angle tests, and one explained threshold or servo-range adjustment.
audit_issues: The objective describes wiring and programming the extension build rather than the sensor-threshold-actuator learning.
records.evidence_basis: The extension requires wiring and testing servo angles, selecting light thresholds, testing under classroom conditions, and correcting range faults.

records.module_name: SW5 · Save the Day with Smart Electronics
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 4 Advanced Inputs and Outputs
records.objective: Students will apply modular troubleshooting and user testing to refine a multi-input/output prototype for a specific learner need.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Educational-toy worksheet and working prototype, checkpoint, individual module tests, silent user-test evidence, and one revision tied to the learner's response.
audit_issues: The objective lists the components in the prototype rather than the systems-design and user-testing learning.
The design-process evidence supports §126.19(c)(3)(B), which is more precise than treating the lesson only as algorithm work.
records.evidence_basis: The extension requires testing each component separately, defining what the toy teaches, testing with an unexplained user, and changing the prototype when the interaction is unclear.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: SPIKE PRIME Day 1 — Help! Find the Problem
records.objective: Students will explain how a specific problem statement and measurable success criteria guide an engineering design process.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Problem-definition sheet with the user, problem, why it matters, and 2–3 measurable criteria, plus the exit sentence connecting the problem to one criterion.
audit_issues: The current objective lists what students produce. The revised objective names the design-process understanding proved by that work.
records.evidence_basis: Linked Day 1 assignment requires a problem statement, measurable success criteria, and a reflective sentence.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: SPIKE PRIME Days 2–3 — Hopper Race
records.objective: Students will analyze comparable test data to justify how changing one design variable affects prototype performance.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Prototype Log with baseline and two iterations, comparable times, one changed variable per trial, and a written claim citing the data.
audit_issues: The current objective is the procedure. The revised objective makes analysis and justification the learning target.
records.evidence_basis: Linked Hopper Race assignment requires three timed prototypes, one-variable changes, and a reflection comparing results.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: SPIKE PRIME Days 4–5 — Super Cleanup
records.objective: Students will evaluate two designs with consistent criteria and repeated test data, then justify which design better fits a specific job.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed grabber data table and a two-sentence recommendation that cites a specific result and names the job the selected design fits.
audit_issues: The current objective mostly restates the testing activity. The revised objective identifies evaluation and evidence-based recommendation as the learning.
records.evidence_basis: Linked Super Cleanup assignment requires fair-test criteria, repeated trials, a data table, and a recommendation citing the table.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: SPIKE PRIME Extension — Design for You
records.objective: Students will apply user-centered design to explain how prototype features address a specific desk problem.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Prototype photo and two sentences naming the user problem, one purposeful feature, and evidence from a test or observation that the feature helps.
audit_issues: The current objective combines three completion actions. The revised objective states the user-centered design understanding those actions should prove.
records.evidence_basis: Linked extension asks students to identify an annoying desk problem, build a helper, and explain the design.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AR Lesson 1 — AR Basics and the MergeCube
records.objective: Students will explain how augmented reality differs from virtual reality and apply familiar 3D-design knowledge in a newly encountered AR tool.
records.demonstration_of_learning: EdPuzzle response that accurately distinguishes AR from VR, plus a working astronaut name-tag cube link or screenshot with all required faces customized.
audit_issues: The current objective mixes a conceptual distinction with the build checklist. The revised objective foregrounds transfer of learning and the DOL preserves both forms of evidence.
records.evidence_basis: The guide’s launch collects the AR/VR distinction, and the linked build requires students to transfer familiar text, image, and 3D-object skills to Delightex.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AR Lesson 2 — AR Worlds
records.objective: Students will apply a design plan to explain how consistent setting and language choices make two AR scenes feel like one coherent world.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed planet/language planning worksheet and two-scene Delightex link in which a peer can identify the repeated setting and language choices.
audit_issues: The current objective is a construction task and the current TEKS does not capture the visible planning evidence. The revision aligns the planned multimedia world to the design process.
records.evidence_basis: The guide requires paper planning, two related scenes, visible world/language details, and a peer coherence check.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AR Lesson 3 — Interactive AR Shopping
records.objective: Students will analyze and improve event-action logic so each customer click produces the intended shopping path.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Three-scene shopping link plus a partner route test showing every click works, with one documented correction if a route initially failed.
audit_issues: The current objective states what to build. The revised objective identifies algorithm analysis, testing, and improvement as the learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide has students trace click events, sketch the customer path, build, peer-test, and repair click behavior.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: AR Lesson 4 — Interactive AR Game Design
records.objective: Students will apply and improve event and physics logic so an AR game’s goal, rules, and feedback work reliably for a player.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Playable AR game link and playtest checklist showing a clear goal, functioning physics, purposeful parts, and one troubleshooting decision or revision.
audit_issues: The current objective is primarily the product specification. The revised objective identifies the algorithmic and troubleshooting learning proved by a playable game.
records.evidence_basis: The guide explicitly models physics logic, requires partner playtesting, and checks goal, rules, feedback, and repaired failures.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: 360 Images and Scenes
records.objective: Students will analyze how 360 imagery and modeled 3D space represent the same place differently, then select media and tools that support navigation.
records.demonstration_of_learning: One Delightex link containing the completed 360-photo scene and corresponding navigable 3D scene, plus a short comparison naming one strength of each representation.
audit_issues: The current objective lists import and build actions while the DOL only checks existence. The revision adds the comparison needed to prove purposeful media selection.
records.evidence_basis: The guide links a 360-photo scene and a rebuilt 3D scene; the module audit identifies combined formats, tool selection, and design process as visible evidence.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: VR Lesson 1 — Delightex Basics
records.objective: Students will apply prior 3D-design knowledge to explain how objects, animation, camera movement, floor, and labels shape navigation in a new VR environment.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Delightex share link with all five named features and a brief partner check identifying how one feature helps a visitor navigate or understand the scene.
audit_issues: The current objective is a feature checklist. The revised objective makes transfer to a newly encountered technology and purposeful tool use explicit.
records.evidence_basis: The guide models each feature, requires partner navigation, and checks whether a partner can locate animation and camera movement.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: VR Lesson 3 — VR Novel Retelling
records.topic: Narrative design for an immersive audience
records.objective: Students will apply narrative structure and iterative design to translate a novel into a coherent three-scene VR experience for an audience.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Storyboard and three-scene Delightex link, followed by peer feedback and one documented revision that improves narrative clarity or navigation.
audit_issues: The current objective centers on completing and sharing the build. The revised objective names the narrative translation and iterative-design learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide requires a storyboard, multimedia scene elements, a showcase, feedback, revision, and final VR evidence.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Pitching Lesson 0 — Logo Design Launch
records.topic: Visual communication principles in logo design
records.objective: Students will explain how simplicity, color, and symbolism help a logo communicate identity.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed EdPuzzle responses and one design intention that names a principle the student will apply in the next lesson.
audit_issues: The current objective asks students to identify a future choice but does not state the communication concept learned. This remains a preparation lesson with no independent TEKS claim.
records.evidence_basis: The guide uses logo comparison, video questions, and a debrief connecting design principles to the next lesson; it explicitly labels the item as preparation.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Pitching Lesson 1 — Personal Logo and Brand
records.objective: Students will apply visual communication principles to justify how a name, meaningful icon, and limited color palette communicate personal identity.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed worksheet and accessible Adobe Express logo link, including a brief explanation of what the icon and color choices communicate.
audit_issues: The current objective is the logo specification. The revised objective identifies application and justification as the learning, while the DOL keeps the authentic product.
records.evidence_basis: The guide requires planning, a meaningful icon, three-color restraint, a working share link, and the sentence stem explaining the icon’s meaning.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Pitching Lesson 2 — Personal Brand Video
records.objective: Students will explain and apply how text, images, a logo, and music work together to communicate a coherent personal identity to an audience.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Published personal-brand video and worksheet share link meeting the content requirements, plus a short explanation of one multimedia choice and its intended audience effect.
audit_issues: The current objective is a list of required components. The revised objective states the multimedia communication learning that the final video must demonstrate.
records.evidence_basis: The guide models combined media, requires publishing and non-owner link testing, and uses peer/teacher checks for coherence and completeness.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Tech for Good Capstone — Research, Build, Test, and Showcase
records.objective: Students will evaluate and refine a technology-for-good solution by using research, testing evidence, and feedback to justify design decisions.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Chosen project artifact, credible-source research notes with citations, test or feedback evidence, one documented refinement, and final reflection explaining how the evidence shaped the solution.
audit_issues: The current objective is the full project workflow. The revised objective identifies evaluation, refinement, and evidence-based justification as the capstone learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide requires credible research, an approved plan, a working artifact, peer or user testing, revision, showcase, and portfolio reflection.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Capstone Close — Scholarship Profile Check-in
records.objective: Students will apply grade-level filters to interpret which scholarship matches are relevant to their current eligibility.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Readable screenshot of grade-filtered Xello matches and one sentence naming a relevant match or explaining why the current results are limited.
audit_issues: The current objective only states account actions. The revision adds interpretation while preserving the guide’s honest no-TEKS operational status.
records.evidence_basis: The run card requires profile completion, grade filtering, and a screenshot while explicitly avoiding an independent TEKS claim.

records.module_name: SW6 · Closing: ePortfolio and Post Survey
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Closing Lesson 1 — Publish the ePortfolio
records.objective: Students will evaluate and curate project evidence to communicate their growth and technical learning to an authentic audience using appropriate digital etiquette.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Published Adobe Express portfolio link that opens for a non-owner and includes the required projects, meaningful descriptions, personal logo, and at least one reflection on growth.
audit_issues: The current objective is publication-focused. The revised objective names evaluation, curation, audience communication, and growth as the learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide requires gathering work, planning sections, publishing, non-owner link testing, descriptions, and a checklist of portfolio evidence.

records.module_name: SW6 · Closing: ePortfolio and Post Survey
records.title: Facilitator Guide: Closing Lesson 2 — Post-Survey
records.objective: Students will reflect on their course experience and independently communicate accurate feedback.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed confidential Canvas post-survey recorded in Canvas.
audit_issues: The current objective is only the completion action. The revision names reflection and independent communication while retaining the explicit no-TEKS operational status.
records.evidence_basis: The run card protects privacy, requires independent responses, and treats completion status rather than response content as the observable evidence.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Stop Motion Lesson 0 — Process Video and Setup
records.objective: Students will explain the planning, filming, and editing sequence used to produce a readable stop-motion film.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed 10-question EdPuzzle and one filming-quality takeaway connecting the video to the upcoming project.
audit_issues: The current objective uses identify at a low DOK and the DOL only records completion. The revision requires students to explain the production sequence without inventing a TEKS claim for this preparation lesson.
records.evidence_basis: The guide maps the video to plan, plot, storyboard, film, and edit, and already calls for one filming-quality takeaway.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Stop Motion Day 1 — Story Plan
records.objective: Students will analyze story scope and justify how a character, setting, conflict, and resolution can be shown in a short animation.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Submitted paragraph, list, or mind map identifying all four story elements and one sentence explaining why the story is filmable within the project limits.
audit_issues: The current objective is the story-plan checklist. The revised objective names scope analysis and justification as the planning learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide compares filmable and oversized ideas, conferences for manageable scope, and requires all four story decisions.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Stop Motion Day 2 — Plot Diagram
records.objective: Students will apply narrative structure to organize a coherent sequence from exposition through resolution for production.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Submitted five-part plot diagram in an allowed format, with a partner check that correctly identifies the climax and traces the conflict to its resolution.
audit_issues: The current objective names the five boxes to complete. The revised objective identifies coherent sequencing as the learning proved by the diagram.
records.evidence_basis: The guide models a plot mountain, requires all five stages, and uses a partner check to test the conflict sequence.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Stop Motion Day 3 — Storyboard
records.objective: Students will translate a plot into an ordered visual plan that communicates camera, action, movement, and material needs to a production partner.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Submitted 6–12-scene storyboard and materials list that a partner can follow without additional explanation.
audit_issues: The current objective is a scene-count task. The revised objective states the communication and production-planning learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide turns plot moments into scenes and checks order, action, movement, props, and partner readability.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Stop Motion Days 4–6 — Film, Edit, and Submit
records.objective: Students will evaluate and revise technical and narrative choices so a stop-motion film communicates clearly to an audience.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Final 30–60 second video that opens, plus peer-check or self-score evidence identifying one revision to stability, lighting, story clarity, sound, or titles.
audit_issues: The current objective is the final product specification. The revised objective names evaluation and revision, which the production and peer-review process can demonstrate.
records.evidence_basis: The guide includes production, peer review, re-shooting, export, upload, and self-scoring against story and technical-quality criteria.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 1 Project 1 Overview
records.objective: Students will explain how empathy, ideation, prototyping, testing, feedback, and revision work together to produce a circuit solution for a user.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Lesson 1 checkpoint or project plan that identifies the user need and correctly sequences the design stages the team will use.
audit_issues: The current objective summarizes the whole project’s actions and the DOL lists end-of-project artifacts. A daily overview guide needs evidence available in this lesson.
records.evidence_basis: The guide links three overview presentations and a Lesson 1 checkpoint; the module-level audit confirms the full project demonstrates the design process.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 2 Empathize and Define
records.topic: User evidence and circuit problem definition
records.objective: Students will analyze user information to define a specific circuit-system need and measurable success criteria.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed Empathize and Define worksheet that includes user evidence, a focused problem statement, and success criteria.
audit_issues: The current objective is close but focuses on gathering and completing. The revision raises the target to analysis and makes success criteria explicit for later testing.
records.evidence_basis: The lesson’s named worksheet captures empathize and define evidence for the Snap Circuits project.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 3 Ideate and Prototype
records.objective: Students will compare circuit ideas against user criteria and justify a prototype choice before building and troubleshooting it.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Ideation evidence comparing options, a short justification for the selected design, and a working Snap Circuits prototype ready for testing.
audit_issues: The current objective lists develop, select, and build actions. The revised objective identifies comparison and justification as the learning that makes the prototype meaningful evidence.
records.evidence_basis: The guide links the ideation/prototype lesson and rubric; the module audit identifies design process and troubleshooting as evidenced.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 4 Test and Submit
records.objective: Students will evaluate circuit test evidence, diagnose a problem, and justify a revision that improves the prototype against its criteria.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed Test and Submit worksheet, prototype evidence, documented problem, before-and-after revision evidence, and final submission.
audit_issues: The current objective is the test-submit procedure. The revised objective names evaluation, diagnosis, and justification as the mastery target.
records.evidence_basis: The guide explicitly requires testing, a documented problem, a useful revision, and final evidence.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 1 Robot Salad For Sale
records.objective: Students will analyze spreadsheet calculations of cost, revenue, and profit, then use the results to justify a business advertising decision.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed project worksheet with accurate cost, revenue, and profit calculations, plus an advertisement whose price or message is justified by those results.
audit_issues: The current objective combines calculate and create actions but does not state the decision-making learning connecting the two products.
records.evidence_basis: The module audit and guide identify spreadsheet calculations and a business advertisement as the paired evidence.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 1 Project 2 Overview
records.objective: Students will explain how a user need, algorithm, prototype testing, feedback, and revision work together in a programmed design process.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Lesson 1 checkpoint or project plan that identifies the intended user, need, planned micro:bit behavior, and how the solution will be tested.
audit_issues: The current objective summarizes every project action and the DOL lists the eventual project bundle. A daily overview needs learning and evidence available in Lesson 1.
records.evidence_basis: The guide links three overview presentations and a checkpoint; later lessons separately produce prototype, feedback, and final evidence.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 2 Project 2 Empathize and Define
records.topic: User evidence and micro:bit problem definition
records.objective: Students will analyze user information to define a specific need and measurable success criteria for a micro:bit solution.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed Empathize and Define worksheet with user evidence, a focused problem statement, and measurable success criteria.
audit_issues: The current objective identifies and defines but does not make the analysis or test criteria explicit.
records.evidence_basis: The lesson’s project-specific worksheet is the observable empathize/define evidence used by later design stages.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 3 Project 2 Ideate
records.objective: Students will compare feature and behavior ideas, then justify a micro:bit prototype plan that can meet the user criteria.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Ideate worksheet containing compared ideas, a selected prototype sketch, planned micro:bit behavior, materials budget, and a short selection justification.
audit_issues: The current objective is a list of sketch, compare, and plan actions. The revision identifies comparison and justification as the learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide’s evidence already includes the sketch, planned behavior, and budget; adding the choice rationale ties the artifact to the objective.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 4 Project 2 Prototype
records.objective: Students will apply algorithm development and debugging to make a micro:bit prototype behave as planned for its user need, then justify a revision.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Working micro:bit prototype, program evidence, and a before-and-after test record explaining one code or design revision.
audit_issues: The current objective states build, test, and revise actions. The revision names algorithm development, debugging, and justification as the learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide requires a working prototype, program evidence, and at least one documented test or revision.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 5 Project 2 Test Share Submit
records.objective: Students will evaluate user feedback and test results to justify a code or design revision that improves a micro:bit solution.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed testing-and-feedback worksheet, revised prototype or program, and final submission with one sentence connecting the evidence to the revision.
audit_issues: The current objective is the test-share-submit procedure. The revision makes evaluation and evidence-based improvement the learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide names testing with another person, feedback, revision, and final project evidence.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Project 3 Overview
records.objective: Students will explain how user need, system planning, prototyping, testing, feedback, and revision work together in a smart-electronics design process.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Lesson 1 checkpoint or project plan identifying the end user, need, intended input/output behavior, and planned test.
audit_issues: The current objective compresses the whole project workflow and the DOL lists end-of-project artifacts. A daily overview needs lesson-level evidence.
records.evidence_basis: The guide links three overview presentations and a checkpoint; later guides separately teach and assess each design stage.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 2 Project 3 Empathize and Define
records.topic: User evidence and smart-electronics problem definition
records.objective: Students will analyze end-user information to define a specific smart-electronics need and measurable success criteria.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed Empathize and Define worksheet with end-user evidence, a focused problem statement, and measurable success criteria.
audit_issues: The current objective is close but states identify and define actions without the analysis and test criteria needed to prove design understanding.
records.evidence_basis: The named worksheet is the project evidence for the empathize/define stage.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 3 Project 3 Ideate
records.objective: Students will compare possible input, output, and feature choices, then justify a prototype plan that can meet the user criteria.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Ideate worksheet with compared ideas, selected system sketch, planned input/output behavior, materials budget, and a short selection justification.
audit_issues: The current objective is a sketch-and-budget task. The revision identifies system comparison and design justification as the learning.
records.evidence_basis: The guide’s current evidence includes a prototype sketch, planned system behavior, and materials budget.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 4 Project 3 Prototype
records.objective: Students will apply algorithmic reasoning and troubleshooting to explain how inputs, code, and outputs work together, then revise a system failure.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Working smart-electronics prototype, program or wiring evidence, labeled input-to-output explanation, and before-and-after evidence of one test or revision.
audit_issues: The current objective lists build, test, and revise actions. The revision makes system reasoning and troubleshooting the mastery target.
records.evidence_basis: The guide requires input/output testing, program or wiring evidence, and a documented problem or revision.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 5 Project 3 Feedback
records.objective: Students will evaluate end-user feedback against success criteria and justify one improvement to the smart-electronics prototype.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Completed feedback worksheet with end-user evidence, the criterion affected, one documented prototype improvement, and a brief justification.
audit_issues: The current objective is the feedback procedure. The revision identifies evaluation against criteria and justification as the learning; troubleshooting TEKS is removed unless technical diagnosis is actually evidenced.
records.evidence_basis: The lesson collects end-user testing and requires one improvement in response to feedback.

records.title: Facilitator Guide: Lesson 6 Project 3 Pitch and Submit
records.objective: Students will justify how a final smart-electronics solution addresses the user need by using evidence from planning, testing, feedback, and revision.
records.demonstration_of_learning: Final pitch and functioning prototype demonstration, supported by complete project artifacts and one explanation connecting test or feedback evidence to a design decision.
audit_issues: The current objective is a presentation and submission checklist. The revision names evidence-based design justification as the learning proved by the pitch.
records.evidence_basis: The guide requires the user need, final solution, prototype evidence, full artifacts, and final pitch/submission.
